  "cut_point": "We are given:

$$
\sin \alpha = 1 - \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ \sin \alpha
$$

### Step 1: Rearranging the equation

Bring all terms to one side:

$$
\sin \alpha + \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ \sin \alpha = 1
$$

Factor out $\sin \alpha$:

$$
\sin \alpha (1 + \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ) = 1
$$

### Step 2: Use the identity for $\tan 10^\circ$

We know that:

$$
\tan 10^\circ = \frac{\sin 10^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ}
$$

Substitute this into the equation:

$$
\sin \alpha \left(1 + \sqrt{3} \cdot \frac{\sin 10^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ} \right) = 1
$$

$$
\sin \alpha \left( \frac{\cos 10^\circ + \sqrt{3} \sin 10^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ} \right) = 1
$$

Multiply both sides by $\cos 10^\circ$:

$$
\sin \alpha \left( \cos 10^\circ + \sqrt{3} \sin 10^\circ \right) = \cos 10^\circ
$$

### Step 3: Recognize the trigonometric identity

We can simplify the expression in the numerator:

$$
\cos 10^\circ + \sqrt{3} \sin 10^\circ
$$

This is the form of the cosine of an angle minus 10°, which is:

$$
\cos(60^\circ - 10^\circ) = \cos 50^\circ
$$",

annotation.cut_point:
We are given:

$$
\sin \alpha = 1 - \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ \sin \alpha
$$

### Step 1: Rearranging the equation

Bring all terms to one side:

$$
\sin \alpha + \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ \sin \alpha = 1
$$

Factor out $\sin \alpha$:

$$
\sin \alpha (1 + \sqrt{3} \tan 10^\circ) = 1
$$

### Step 2: Use the identity for $\tan 10^\circ$

We know that:

$$
\tan 10^\circ = \frac{\sin 10^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ}
$$

Substitute this into the equation:

$$
\sin \alpha \left(1 + \sqrt{3} \cdot \frac{\sin 10^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ} \right) = 1
$$

$$
\sin \alpha \left( \frac{\cos 10^\circ + \sqrt{3} \sin 10^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ} \right) = 1
$$

Multiply both sides by $\cos 10^\circ$:

$$
\sin \alpha \left( \cos 10^\circ + \sqrt{3} \sin 10^\circ \right) = \cos 10^\circ
$$

### Step 3: Recognize the trigonometric identity

We can simplify the expression in the numerator:

$$
\cos 10^\circ + \sqrt{3} \sin 10^\circ
$$

This is the form of the cosine of an angle minus 10°, which is:

$$
\cos(60^\circ - 10^\circ) = \cos 50^\circ
$$
